turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, give me a sec, this login's been playing up all arvo. Right. What's brought you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, I'm just so tired. Properly wiped out. And I get puffed really easy.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Puffed, sorry, say that again? The screen just jumped on me.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Breathless. Stairs at home, I'm puffing halfway up. I don't know, doctor, how long it's been.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'm her sister, I stay a few nights a week. It's been months. I hear her stop on the stairs.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the tiredness, can you date that at all?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Maybe the same sort of time. I can't put a date on it.
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Tell him about the periods. That's what's been awful.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. They're heavy, and they drag on for eight or nine days. Been like that for about a year, I reckon.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Heavy how? I'm pulling the file up, bear with me if I ask twice.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Pads. I don't know exactly. Four or five a day? More on the bad days. I lose count.
[SEG0012] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Some days she changes one and it's already soaked through. Those days it's more than four or five.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Clots with that?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. I don't know the size. Like a fifty-cent piece? Bigger sometimes. I try not to look.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any bleeding between the periods, or after sex?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that. Just the period itself.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): And with the breathlessness, any chest pain?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain. No.
[SEG0019] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She goes light-headed if she stands up too quick, though. I've seen it.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Sometimes, yeah. Not every time. I don't know if it matters.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): There's a scribble here about hair and I can't read my own typing. What's that about?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): It's falling out. Shower, hairbrush, heaps more than it used to.
[SEG0023] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I've been picking it off the bathroom tiles. A few months, at least.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Are you taking iron?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Sometimes. When I remember. Got it from the chemist.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Notes on here say Ferro-Gradumet, 325 milligrams, once a day. That what you've got?
[SEG0027] person_3 (CAREGIVER): That's not what the bottle says. It says 105 milligrams. And she was meant to take it daily but she doesn't.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor, which number's right. I take one when I think of it. Not every day. A few times a week, maybe.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the dose on the bottle again? It's kicked me back to the login screen.
[SEG0030] person_3 (CAREGIVER): One hundred and five. The 325 might be an old script, I don't know.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll leave that dose unclear till someone brings the box in. Anything else, pain relief, the pill?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Not on the pill. Um, Nurofen for the cramps. Usually two of the 200s, just on the heavy days.
[SEG0033] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Mum had a thyroid problem. Overactive, and then they took it out, or something like that. Might run in the family.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Your mother. Has anyone checked your thyroid?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): They did bloods. March, I think, or maybe April. They said the iron was borderline. Didn't give me a number.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Borderline. And you're not sure they even did the thyroid?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. I don't think they did. They just said borderline and sent me off.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Weight changing, feeling cold, bowels constipated?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): A bit cold lately. Not constipated. Weight's about the same, I think.
[SEG0040] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She's paler than she was at Christmas, you can see it in her face.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): You do look a bit pale, yes. I should do a blood pressure but the cuff's in the other room and this computer's eaten the appointment.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Last time they said the pressure was fine. I don't remember the figure.

[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright. Working impression, this may be iron deficiency from the heavy periods. That's provisional, I want the bloods before I'd call it. Thyroid's still possible, I wouldn't rule it out.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll order a full blood count, iron studies, and a TSH. Path lab downstairs, this week, no booking needed.
[SEG0045] person_3 (CAREGIVER): What about a scan? She's been worried it's something in the uterus.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): We might do a pelvic ultrasound if the bleeding stays this heavy, or if the bloods don't explain it. I'm not booking that today.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): And do I keep taking the iron? I don't know, doctor. I could write the pads down, I suppose, if I remember.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep taking one tablet from that bottle on the days you remember. Don't double up to catch up. Jot the pad count for one cycle if you can, even roughly.
[SEG0049] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll remind her. She bins the packet and forgets.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Work's been hard too. I'm on the front desk at the school and I'm useless by lunch. Sorry, that's probably not medical.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): It fits with the tiredness, actually. Come back in a fortnight when the results should be in.
[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): And don't wait that long if you're soaking a pad every hour, or you feel like you'll faint.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): OK. I don't know if I'll remember all of it, but I won't wait if it's pouring or I feel faint.

features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
